title: Financial markets and institutions
audience: a college student in a finance, accounting or business degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Explain how money, bond, stock, derivative and foreign-exchange markets work; how banks, insurers, pension funds, mutual funds, ETFs and hedge funds create value and manage risk; how trading, clearing and settlement work; and how central banks and regulators supervise the financial system.
primary_reading: Open Yale Courses: ECON 252 Financial Markets, taught by Robert Shiller (free)

weeks.1: The financial system and its functions
weeks.2: Interest rates and the term structure
weeks.5: Stock markets: exchanges, orders and trading
weeks.7: Commercial banks: balance sheets and risks
weeks.10: Funds: mutual funds, ETFs, hedge funds and private equity

blocks.deliverable: Explain three yield curve shapes and their causes.
Compare Treasury bills, commercial paper and repos.
Trace an order from placement to settlement.
Week 7 midterm; analyze a bank balance sheet.
Compare the fees and structures of three funds.
Explain one historical crisis and the reforms it led to.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Institution report: choose a large bank, insurer or asset manager, read its annual report, explain its business model, main risks and regulators, compare it with a competitor on five measures, and write a four-page report.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
